traceability.evidence: Story file docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md defines requirements REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS with acceptance criteria focused on validating @story file references, clear error messages, safe filesystem handling, configuration, and documentation.,Rule implementation: src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - Uses context.cwd (falling back to process.cwd) for path resolution, matching the story’s Implementation Details. - Parses comments via context.getSourceCode().getAllComments(), splits comment text into lines, and processes lines starting with '@story' (handleComment and validateStoryPath), satisfying REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION. - Resolves paths using normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs) from storyReferenceUtils with configurable storyDirectories and default ["docs/stories", "stories"], satisfying REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION and REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS. - Enforces security with performSecurityValidations (absolute path checks, traversal checking using path.resolve and cwd boundary), and delegates project-boundary checks to handleProjectBoundaryForExistence, satisfying REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION and REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY. - Calls hasValidExtension and reports messageId 'invalidExtension' when requireStoryExtension is true and path does not end in .story.md, matching the extension requirement. - Calls reportExistenceProblems which uses normalizeStoryPath + getStoryExistence to determine existence; reportExistenceStatus maps status 'missing' to messageId 'fileMissing' and 'fs-error' to 'fileAccessError' including the error message, satisfying REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE and REQ-ERROR-HANDLING. - Exposes meta.messages with clear, specific diagnostics: * fileMissing: "Story file '{{path}}' not found" * invalidExtension: "Invalid story file extension for '{{path}}', expected '.story.md'" * invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{path}}'" * fileAccessError: "Could not validate story file '{{path}}' due to a filesystem error: {{error}}. Please check file existence and permissions." These align with the User Experience and Error Handling acceptance criteria.,Helper implementation: src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts - analyzeCandidateBoundaries(candidates, cwd) and handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(...) use enforceProjectBoundary to ensure all candidate and matched paths stay under the project root; if all candidates are outside, they report invalidPath, satisfying REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY and REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS. - performSecurityValidations(...) enforces: * Absolute paths are rejected when allowAbsolute is false, via path.isAbsolute and reportInvalidPath. * For any path containing traversal or separators, it resolves against cwd and rejects if the resolved path does not start with cwd + path.sep. This satisfies REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION and contributes to REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY.,Core utilities: src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs) builds candidate absolute paths: * For './' or '../' paths, resolves directly against cwd. * For bare paths, first resolves under cwd, then under each configured storyDirectories directory using path.basename(storyPath). This implements REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION and REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS. - checkSingleCandidate(candidate) wraps fs.existsSync and fs.statSync in try/catch, distinguishes 'exists', 'missing', and 'fs-error' states, and caches results in fileExistStatusCache (a Map). This satisfies REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, and REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION. - getStoryExistence(candidates) iterates candidates, returns first 'exists' match, otherwise prefers the first 'fs-error' over a generic 'missing' status, preserving error details. This provides robust error vs missing distinction for REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE and REQ-ERROR-HANDLING. - storyExists(paths) returns a boolean based on getStoryExistence, maintaining a simple API while leveraging the richer status model. - normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs) composes buildStoryCandidates and getStoryExistence to return { candidates, exists, existence }, supporting path resolution, existence checks, and performance via caching, matching REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, and REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION. - enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd) checks that normalized candidate paths are under the normalized cwd, implementing REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY. - isAbsolutePath, containsPathTraversal, isTraversalUnsafe, hasValidExtension, and isUnsafeStoryPath encapsulate security and extension checks, satisfying REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION.,Tests specifically for this story: tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts - File header explicitly references this story and its requirements: * @story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md * @req REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE and @supports docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS - "Valid Story Reference Rule (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" RuleTester suite: * valid cases include: - "[REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE] valid story file reference" with code `// @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md`. - "[REQ-EXTENSION] valid .story.md extension" verifying correct extension. - "[REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION] valid relative path with ./ prefix" verifying relative path resolution. * invalid cases include: - "[REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION] missing file" expecting messageId 'fileMissing' with path 'docs/stories/missing-file.story.md' (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE). - "[REQ-EXTENSION] invalid extension" expecting messageId 'invalidExtension' for a .md path (extension enforcement). - "[REQ-PATH-SECURITY] path traversal" with '../outside.story.md' expecting 'invalidPath'. - "[REQ-ABSOLUTE-PATH] absolute path not allowed" with '/etc/passwd.story.md' expecting 'invalidPath'. These tests cover the core functionality, extension checking, path resolution, and security validation requirements.,Configuration and boundary tests within tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts - Configurable paths: * "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] honors custom storyDirectories using docs/stories" uses options { storyDirectories: ["docs/stories"] } with a bare filename plus a normal docs/stories path, verifying storyDirectories resolution (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION). * "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] allowAbsolutePaths accepts existing absolute .story.md inside project" verifies that when allowAbsolutePaths: true and storyDirectories: ["docs/stories"], an absolute path inside the project root is treated as valid, satisfying REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS and REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY. * "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] disallows absolute paths when allowAbsolutePaths is false" confirms absolute paths are rejected when not explicitly allowed (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). * "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] accepts .story.md story path when requireStoryExtension is false (still valid and existing)" plus a separate test "requireStoryExtension=false accepts existing .md story file" validate the behavior of requireStoryExtension and storyDirectories for both .story.md and other .md files (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - Project boundary and misconfiguration: * "[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] story reference outside project root is rejected when discovered via absolute path" passes an absolute path under a fake outside-project root plus a storyDirectories config pointing there, expecting messageId 'invalidPath'. This confirms enforceProjectBoundary and handleProjectBoundaryForExistence prevent external files from being treated as valid (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). * "[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] storyDirectories cannot escape project even when normalize resolves outside cwd" and "[REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY] misconfigured storyDirectories outside project cannot validate external files" assert that even when storyDirectories or candidates point outside the project, diagnostics are produced and invalidPath is reported, rather than silently accepting them (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION).,Error handling tests for filesystem edge cases: tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts - Suite "Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling (Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION)" exercises storyExists and the rule’s error reporting: * "[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] storyExists returns false when fs throws" mocks fs.existsSync and fs.statSync to throw EACCES and verifies storyExists does not throw and returns false (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). * "[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] storyExists returns false when fs.statSync throws EIO and existsSync is true" covers another failure mode (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). * "[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] rule reports fileAccessError when fs.statSync throws and existsSync is true" mocks these operations and verifies diagnostics include messageId 'fileAccessError' with error text containing 'EIO'. * "[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] rule reports fileAccessError when fs throws" similarly asserts 'fileAccessError' with error text containing 'EACCES'. - These tests validate that filesystem/network/permission issues are surfaced as clear, specific diagnostics instead of uncaught exceptions, satisfying the Error Handling acceptance criterion and REQ-ERROR-HANDLING.,Documentation for this rule in user-facing docs: user-docs/api-reference.md - Section "traceability/valid-story-reference" (lines ~160–220): * Description: "Checks that the file paths in `@story` annotations point to existing story markdown files." * Documents options: storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension with defaults and behavior matching the implementation. * Provides example configuration JSON using storyDirectories ["docs/stories", "stories"], allowAbsolutePaths: false, requireStoryExtension: true, exactly as described in the story’s Configuration Integration example. * Shows an example JSDoc with an @story reference. - This fulfills the Documentation acceptance criterion (file validation specification with path resolution rules, options, and usage examples) and aligns with the Implementation Notes in the story.,Integration and quality standards - traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md are implemented and verified. The traceability/valid-story-reference rule, its helpers, and shared utilities provide path resolution from context.cwd, configurable storyDirectories, strict .story.md extension enforcement (configurable), project-boundary and security checks, filesystem error handling with clear diagnostics (fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, fileAccessError), and in-memory caching of filesystem checks. Comprehensive tests in tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts cover valid and invalid paths, configuration options, project boundary behavior, and filesystem error scenarios. User-facing documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md documents this rule’s behavior and configuration. All relevant tests pass under `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose`, so this story is fully implemented and passing.
